primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome due to NLRP3 gain of function
mechanism: Gain-of-function NLRP3 variants cause excessive assembly/activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, increasing caspase-1-dependent maturation of proinflammatory cytokines, particularly IL-1 beta and IL-18. This produces the spectrum of cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes.
vignette: A 22-year-old woman has recurrent episodes of fever, urticaria-like rash, and arthralgia that are triggered by cold exposure. She has progressive sensorineural hearing loss, and her mother had similar symptoms. Genetic testing identifies a heterozygous gain-of-function variant in NLRP3.
lead: Which of the following molecular consequences most directly explains this disorder?
correct: Excessive inflammasome activation with increased caspase-1-mediated maturation of interleukin-1 beta
distractors: Failure of complement C1 inhibitor to restrain kallikrein-mediated bradykinin production
Defective Fas-mediated apoptosis of autoreactive lymphocytes
Loss of NADPH oxidase activity in neutrophil phagosomes
Failure of regulatory T-cell development due to FOXP3 dysfunction
distractor_notes: C1-inhibitor deficiency causes hereditary angioedema, not a cold-triggered NLRP3 autoinflammatory syndrome with hearing loss.
FAS defects cause autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome rather than CAPS.
NADPH oxidase deficiency causes chronic granulomatous disease with recurrent catalase-positive infections.
FOXP3 deficiency causes IPEX syndrome with autoimmunity and enteropathy rather than NLRP3-driven periodic fever.
key_expl: NLRP3 is an intracellular sensor that assembles an inflammasome. Gain-of-function variants cause excessive inflammasome activity, with caspase-1-dependent processing and release of IL-1 beta and IL-18. Cold-triggered episodes and sensorineural hearing loss fit the CAPS spectrum, particularly familial cold autoinflammatory/Muckle-Wells phenotypes.
objective: Link NLRP3 gain of function in CAPS to excessive inflammasome activation and increased caspase-1-mediated IL-1 beta maturation.
